record_type_quote: Reproduction of a research claim from Stanley et al. (2020), in PsyArXiv

targets.authors: Stanley, M., Barr, N., PETERS, K., & Seli, P., Ph.D.
targets.title: Analytic-Thinking Predicts Hoax Beliefs and Helping Behaviors in Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic.
targets.evidence_quote:
Claim summary: We selected the claim that those individuals who perform worse on the
CRT (cognitive reflection test) were less likely to have engaged in helpful behaviors (related
to the covid-19 pandemic) over the prior week. This reflects the following statement from the
paper’s abstract: “Our results indicate that individuals less willing to engage effortful,
deliberative, and reflective cognitive processes were more likely to believe the pandemic
was a hoax, and less likely to have recently engaged in social-distancing and hand-
washing.” The claim was tested by computing bivariate correlations between average CRT
performance and measures of helping behaviors (social-distancing being one of 3 tested).
This analysis yielded that participants who performed worse on the CRT were less likely to
have engaged in social-distancing.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
Reproduction result: The claim was tested by computing bivariate correlations between
average CRT performance and measures of helping behaviors (social-distancing being one
of 3 tested). This analysis yielded a positive correlation, i.e. participants who performed
worse on the CRT were less likely to have engaged in social-distancing (r(276) = .14, p =
.02).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Exploratory findings: No exploratory analyses were conducted.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original and reproduced focal correlation and p value match. Only the original focal analysis is reported; no exploratory or alternative specification analyses were conducted.
